vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mystock
Version: 1.1.2

The 'mystock' skill bundle is a legitimate stock analysis assistant providing a Web UI for real-time quotes, portfolio management, and market analysis. The code integrates with several financial data providers (Tencent, Eastmoney, Sina, and pywencai) and supports multiple AI backends for investment insights. While the installation script performs a global npm installation of 'jsdom' and the FastAPI backend implements a permissive CORS policy (allow_origins=['*']), these are functional requirements or common development configurations rather than indicators of malice. No evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or prompt injection was found across the backend logic, frontend code, or agent instructions.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement a plausible stock assistant, but there are mismatches and risky actions (install script, undocumented credential use, wide-open CORS, global npm installs) that merit caution before running.

dimensions.detail: The code implements the described stock/limit-up/portfolio features (pywencai, FastAPI backend, Vue UI). However the package metadata declared no required env vars or binaries, while the code and docs clearly expect Node.js, global jsdom, and optional AI provider credentials (AI_PROVIDER, AI_API_KEY). That mismatch between declared requirements and actual needs is unexpected.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and README instruct running scripts/install.sh and ./start.sh which will install system-level dependencies (npm global jsdom, set NODE_PATH), set environment variables, start local servers and open a browser. The backend enables CORS allow_origins=['*'] (exposes API to network if host reachable). The instructions also say the installer will "configure environment variables" but do not list what it will write; AI provider keys are referenced elsewhere. These installation/start instructions grant the skill broad discretion on the host.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no registry install spec, but the repository includes scripts/install.sh and start.sh that perform installation and environment configuration. The SKILL.md explicitly tells users to run the install script which will perform global npm installs (npm install -g jsdom) and pip installs. Running an included install.sh that downloads and installs packages globally is higher-risk and should be audited before execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata reported no required env vars, but backend/AI_CONFIG.md and ai_config.py reference AI_PROVIDER and AI_API_KEY and provide instructions for setting them (OpenAI, SiliconFlow, Zhipu). The skill will send chat payloads (including system prompt) to external AI endpoints if configured. The installer promises to "configure environment variables" but doesn't declare which or how. Requesting/using API keys and writing them into .env without declaring them is disproportionate and opaque.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not require always:true and is user-invocable. It starts services that listen on ports (backend 8000, frontend 5000/5001) and sets CORS to '*', so if the host is network-reachable these services could be queried remotely. That network exposure is significant but not an explicit privileged flag in the skill metadata.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package largely does what its description promises (local stock UI + backend), but it contains an install script that modifies the system (global npm installs, sets NODE_PATH, creates/edits env files) and code that will call external AI APIs if you provide keys — yet the registry metadata did not declare those required credentials. Before installing:

- Inspect scripts/install.sh and start.sh line-by-line to see what they install and whether they create or write .env files or other credentials. Do not run them blindly.
- Do not paste secret API keys into a system you don't fully control; check exactly where AI_API_KEY (or other keys) would be stored (environment vs .env) and prefer short-lived/test keys or none at all.
- Run the install/start steps in an isolated environment (VM or container) with limited network access if you want to test.
- Review backend code: it enables CORS '*' and binds servers that could be reachable on your network; restrict access with a firewall or run on localhost-only if possible.
- If you only need chatbot-free functionality, avoid configuring AI_PROVIDER/API keys and verify the application falls back to rule-based mode.
- Consider replacing global npm installs with local installs, and avoid running installers as root.

If you want, I can: (1) summarize the exact operations in scripts/install.sh and start.sh, (2) point out every place the code reads or writes environment variables and files, or (3) produce a safe checklist to run this skill inside a container.
